name: Plank
description: The plank is an isometric core stability exercise in which the body is held in a push-up position with the forearms or hands on the floor. It trains the transverse abdominis, rectus abdominis, and stabilizing muscles of the spine to resist extension, making it fundamental for core stability, lower back health, and athletic performance.

execution.starting_position: Lie face down. Place forearms on the floor with elbows directly below the shoulders. Push up onto the forearms and toes so the body forms a straight line from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Use a mat for forearm comfort. Keep the body in one rigid line — no hip sag or piking.
steps: Squeeze the glutes and brace the core by tightening the abdominals.
Maintain a neutral spine — the head, hips, and heels should form a straight line.
Hold the position for the prescribed duration while breathing normally.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe in and out normally throughout the hold — do not hold your breath.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging downward — squeeze the glutes to prevent this
Hips raised too high, piking at the waist
Neck too low or raised — keep a neutral head position
safety_considerations: If lower back pain occurs, reduce duration or perform on knees
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Isometric hold. No joint movement — maintain the position for the target duration.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Hold for 20–60 seconds per set, progressing duration over time
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes hard — this automatically protects the lower back
Think about pulling your elbows toward your feet — this activates the core further
